Widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the league, he is known for his versatility, shot-blocking, and playmaking. Barnes attended [[Cardinal Newman High School (West Palm Beach, Florida)|Cardinal Newman High School]] in his hometown of [[West Palm Beach, Florida]], before transferring to [[NSU University School]]. He later attended [[Montverde Academy]], where he was rated a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services in his senior year. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] and was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|conference rookie of the year]] in 2021. Selected with the fourth overall pick by the Raptors in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Barnes was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] in 2022. After a relatively disappointing second season, he had a breakout year in 2024, when he received his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] selection and the Raptors pivoted to him as their [[franchise player]]. As the Raptors became competitive again after a [[Tanking|rebuild]], Barnes received his second All-Star selection and his first on an [[All-Defensive team|All-Defensive Team]] in 2026. He is regarded as a versatile player, capable of playmaking, ball-handling, and many defensive functions, although his jump shot has been an area of criticism. == Early life == Barnes was born on August 1, 2001,{{Cite web |year=2026 |title=Scottie Barnes |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1630567/scottie-barnes |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en}} in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]], and was raised alongside three siblings by their mother Kathalyn Wilkins.{{Cite web |last=Sohi |first=Seerat |date=2023-02-01 |title=Is Scottie Barnes Ready to Spread His (Big) Wings? |url=https://www.theringer.com/2023/02/01/nba/scottie-barnes-toronto-raptors-nba-trade-deadline |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |language=en}} Barnes described his upbringing as "pretty hard" as his family did not have stable housing and lived in troublesome neighborhoods.{{Cite news |last=Reed |first=Tashan |date=2020-01-07 |title=‘To me, he’s a no-brainer, high-lottery pick’: Scottie Barnes will arrive at Florida State amid a ton of hype |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1504812/2020/01/07/scottie-barnes-florida-state-2020-basketball-signee-ton-of-hype/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407143831/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1504812/2020/01/07/scottie-barnes-florida-state-2020-basketball-signee-ton-of-hype/ |archive-date=2025-04-07 |access-date=2026-05-26 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} He began playing organized basketball in the third grade in a [[Salvation Army]] league, with a team composed mostly of fourth-graders.{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Deyscha |date=2022-07-29 |title=Scottie Barnes Has Everything it Takes to Become Toronto’s Next Star |url=https://slamonline.com/the-magazine/scottie-barnes-slam-239/ |access-date=2026-06-18 |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |language=en-US |issn=1072-625X}} He also played [[Streetball|pick-up]] at local gyms against opponents much older than him, who he credited for improving his perception and knowledge of the game. As a fifth-grader Barnes caught the attention of [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) youth basketball coach John Simpson, who was invited to join his team, the Wellington Wolves. Simpson and his son Jason developed a close relationship with Barnes, who soon moved in with them in the affluent village of [[Wellington, Florida|Wellington]] so he could reduce the burden on his mother.{{Cite web |last=Wong |first=Alex |date=2025-01-22 |others=Portraits by Luis Mora |title=The Chosen One: At just 23, Scottie Barnes is the new face of the Raptors—and the team’s best chance of salvation |url=https://torontolife.com/deep-dives/scottie-barnes-new-face-of-the-raptors-and-the-teams-best-chance-of-salvation/ |url-access=registration |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250206172330/https://torontolife.com/deep-dives/scottie-barnes-new-face-of-the-raptors-and-the-teams-best-chance-of-salvation/ |archive-date=2025-02-06 |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=[[Toronto Life]] |language=en |issn=0049-4194}} With Barnes, the Wolves went from what Simpson described as a purely casual team to participating in national tournaments.{{Cite news |last=Koreen |first=Eric |date=2021-09-17 |title=‘He gets inspired by inspiring others’: Toronto Raptors rookie Scottie Barnes is the gift that keeps on giving |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2820312/2021/09/17/he-gets-inspired-by-inspiring-others-toronto-raptors-rookie-scottie-barnes-is-the-gift-that-keeps-on-giving/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204023129/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2820312/2021/09/17/he-gets-inspired-by-inspiring-others-toronto-raptors-rookie-scottie-barnes-is-the-gift-that-keeps-on-giving/ |archive-date=2025-12-04 |access-date=2026-05-27 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Already gifted in height, Barnes refined his athleticism and overall game with the Wolves, and by the end of seventh grade he was dominating his opponents. ==High school career== [[File:Scottie Barnes.jpg|left|thumb|260x260px|Barnes at the [[Nike EYBL]] in 2019]] As a freshman in 2016, Barnes played basketball for [[Cardinal Newman High School (West Palm Beach, Florida)|Cardinal Newman High School]] in West Palm Beach. He earned All-Area second team and [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American honors after leading Newman to a 19–8 record and the 5A regional semifinals.{{cite web |last1=Wagner|first1=Jodie|title=Cardinal Newman F Scottie Barnes transfers to University School|url=https://highschoolbuzz.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2017/08/30/boys-basketball-cardinal-newman-f-scottie-barnes-transfers-to-university-school/|website=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|access-date=January 21, 2020|date=August 30, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905094232/http://highschoolbuzz.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2017/08/30/boys-basketball-cardinal-newman-f-scottie-barnes-transfers-to-university-school/|archive-date=2017-09-05|url-status=live}} For his sophomore year Barnes transferred to [[NSU University School]] in Fort Lauderdale, where he was teammates with five-star prospect [[Vernon Carey Jr.]]. Barnes contributed to University School's 36–2 record and a Class 5A state title, averaging 15 points, eight rebounds and six assists per game.{{Cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |date=2021-07-30 |title=Scottie Barnes, former Cardinal Newman and University School star, drafted by the Toronto Raptors |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-barnes-drafted-20210730-zmdokvtuafczvbpy64rgsotq44-story.html |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |language=en-US |agency=[[Sun-Sentinel]]}} University School won a [[City of Palms Classic]] championship with Barnes being named the tournament's [[most valuable player]] (MVP).{{Cite web |last=Kushel |first=Alex |date=2023-07-13 |title=Toronto Raptors player returns to West Palm Beach for youth basketball camp |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2023/07/13/toronto-raptors-player-returns-to-west-palm-beach-for-youth-basketball-camp/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=[[Sun Sentinel]] |language=en-US}} At [[High School Showcase|GEICO Nationals]], he averaged 21.3 points and 9.7 rebounds across the three games as University School surpassed expectations and reached the championship game, where they lost to [[Montverde Academy]]. In his junior season, Barnes averaged 14.5 points, 7.4 rebounds and 5.8 assists per game, him and Carey leading the team to a 27–5 record, a second straight 5A state title, and a second appearance at the GEICO Nationals championship game where they again lost to Montverde Academy. After University School coach James Carr was fired, Barnes decided to transfer to a different school for his senior year. He was convinced by [[Cade Cunningham]] while at a [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|USA under-17]] camp to move to Montverde Academy, which he decided upon in August 2019. With Barnes, Cunningham and [[Day'Ron Sharpe]] among other prospects, many analysts regarded his team as one of the greatest in high school basketball history.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=Why Montverde is being called the best high school basketball team ever |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2020/1/21/21073999/montverde-basketball-roster-cade-cunningham-scottie-barnes-nba-talent-caleb-houstan |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=January 23, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} Barnes averaged 11.6 points, 6.5 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game, contributing to Montverde's 25–0 record and 40-point average margin of victory.{{Cite news |last=Visser |first=David |date=2020-04-03 |title=FSU Basketball Signee Scottie Barnes Reacts to Being a First-Team Sports Illustrated All-American, with Video |url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/basketball/fsu-basketball-signee-scottie-barnes-reacts-first-team-sports-illustrated-all-american-video-highlights |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407154656/https://www.si.com/college/fsu/basketball/fsu-basketball-signee-scottie-barnes-reacts-first-team-sports-illustrated-all-american-video-highlights |archive-date=2020-04-07 |access-date=2026-06-19 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}} He received All-American first team honors from [[MaxPreps]] and ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', becoming one of the most highly-regarded high school prospects in the country. Barnes was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but all three games were canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. ===Recruiting=== A consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Barnes was considered the fourth-best player in the 2020 recruiting class by [[ESPN]]. He was the highest ranked [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in his class by ESPN and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On October 14, 2019, Barnes announced his commitment to play [[college basketball]] for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=5-star recruit Scottie Barnes commits to Florida State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/27844828/5-star-recruit-scottie-barnes-commits-florida-state |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=January 21, 2020 |date=October 14, 2019}} His decision was labeled unusual compared to other prospects as the school was known for prioritizing deep rotations as opposed to letting stars display their prowess. Barnes himself said he "didn't really want to go to a school because of the name," and chose Florida State to participate in their aggressive defensive system.{{Cite news |last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |date=2021-07-30 |title=Scottie Barnes goes to the Toronto Raptors: Here’s what they’re getting |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2721219/2021/07/29/scottie-barnes-goes-to-the-toronto-raptors-heres-what-theyre-getting/ |url-access=limited |access-date=2026-06-18 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Scottie Barnes | position = [[Guard (basketball)|G]] / [[Forward (basketball)|F]] | hometown = [[West Palm Beach, Florida|West Palm Beach, FL]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 240 | 40 = | commitdate = October 14, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Florida State 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Florida State Seminoles Recruiting Class | rivals school = floridastate | scout s = | espn schoolid = 52 | 247 overall = 9 | rivals overall = 7 | espn overall = 5 | accessdate = July 31, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Scottie Barnes Florida State.jpg|thumb|right|305x305px|Barnes with the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Seminoles]] in 2020]]For the [[2020–21 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team]], Barnes played the point guard position off the bench, quickly learning how to operate within the team's offense under head coach [[Leonard Hamilton]]. He served a versatile role on the defensive end, guarding players of all five positions.{{Cite web |last=Loung |first=Steven |date=2021-07-24 |title=Prospect of Interest: Why Scottie Barnes is the best defender in the draft |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/prospect-interest-scottie-barnes-best-defender-draft/ |access-date=2026-06-18 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}} Barnes helped the Seminoles reach the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] championship game, in which he scored a career-high 21 points in an 80–75 loss to [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]],{{cite web |title=Devoe, Georgia Tech beat No. 15 FSU 80-75 for ACC title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401301257 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 13, 2021}} and the Sweet 16 of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a freshman, he averaged 10.3 points, 4.1 assists, 4 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game, earning [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Freshman of the Year]], ACC Sixth Man of the Year and third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] honors. On April 9, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Staley |first1=Antwan |title=Florida State freshman Scottie Barnes declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/nolesports/2021/04/09/florida-state-freshman-scottie-barnes-declares-2021-nba-draft/7166879002/ |website=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=April 9, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2021–present)=== ====Rookie of the Year (2021–22)==== [[File:Scottie Barnes (51914221392) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Barnes at the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game#Skills Challenge|2022]] [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge]]|281x281px]] The [[Toronto Raptors]] selected Barnes with the fourth overall pick of the [[2021 NBA draft|2021 NBA Draft]]. The selection was a surprise to many, as the consensus was the Raptors would select [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] point guard [[Jalen Suggs]].{{Cite web |last=Waters |first=Andres |date=2022-01-11 |title=Toronto Rolled The Dice On Scottie Barnes. It’s Paid Off. |url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/toronto-rolled-the-dice-on-scottie-barnes-its-paid-off/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220323134711/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/toronto-rolled-the-dice-on-scottie-barnes-its-paid-off/ |archive-date=2022-03-23 |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=[[FiveThirtyEight]]}} By the midpoint of the season, ''[[FiveThirtyEight]]'' reported that Barnes was exceeding expectations and proving to be an integral player for the Raptors. He was commonly assigned to defend against star players, meshed well offensively alongside [[Pascal Siakam]] and [[OG Anunoby]], and took secondary ball-handling duties behind [[Fred VanVleet]]. He was generally the third-to-fourth offensive option behind the other starters.{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Doug |date=2022-04-23 |title=Raptor Scottie Barnes, drafted fourth, is the NBA’s rookie of the year: ‘It was a goal of mine’ |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/raptor-scottie-barnes-drafted-fourth-is-the-nba-s-rookie-of-the-year-it-was/article_4c40858c-4d73-551e-a70d-3324d50f778e.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709201925/https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/raptor-scottie-barnes-drafted-fourth-is-the-nba-s-rookie-of-the-year-it-was/article_4c40858c-4d73-551e-a70d-3324d50f778e.html |archive-date=2024-07-09 |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=[[Toronto Star]] |language=en|issn=0319-0781}} He was named to the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|2022]] [[Rising Stars Challenge]], and earned Eastern Conference [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]] honours in February and March.{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=2022-04-23 |title=Toronto Raptors' Scottie Barnes edges Cleveland Cavaliers' Evan Mobley for NBA Rookie of the Year |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33792649/toronto-raptors-forward-scottie-barnes-wins-nba-rookie-year |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}} Playing a total of 74 games, Barnes finished the season averaging 15.3 points, 7.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.1 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game, and shot 49.2% from the field and 30.1% from three-point range. He ranked first among rookies in minutes per game and was the only rookie listed among the top five of all statistical categories.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-04-23 |title=Raptors' Barnes wins Rookie of the Year award |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/scottie-barnes-toronto-raptors-nba-rookie-of-the-year-award-1.1789700 |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |language=en |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}} After a close race with [[Evan Mobley]], Barnes was awarded the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]], the first Raptor to receive the award since [[Vince Carter]] in 1999, and he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-01-31 |title=Raptors' Barnes selected to NBA's Rising Stars Game |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/scottie-barnes-toronto-raptors-selected-to-nba-s-rising-stars-game-1.1913426 |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |language=en}} Spurred by Barnes' impact, the Raptors exceeded expectations and finished as the fifth seed,{{Cite web |last=McGregor |first=Gilbert |date=2022-04-23 |title=Raptors' Scottie Barnes named 2021-22 NBA Rookie of the Year: What's next for Toronto's phenom? |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nba/news/scottie-barnes-raptors-rookie-season/idfcz4ewoija3hpcoygk5chs |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=[[The Sporting News]] |language=en-ca}} facing the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the first round of [[2022 NBA playoffs|the playoffs]]. Barnes suffered a sprained ankle in his playoff debut which forced him to miss the next two games. He averaged 12.8 points, 4.3 assists and 9.0 rebounds in the four playoff games he played as the Raptors were eliminated in six games. ====Second season (2022–23)==== During his second season, Barnes received greater duties regarding playmaking, ball-handling and offence initiation.{{Cite web |last=Loung |first=Steven |date=2023-02-17 |title=Barnes, trio of Canadians headline players to watch at NBA's Rising Stars Game |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/barnes-trio-of-canadians-headline-players-to-watch-at-nbas-rising-stars-game/ |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}} On November 4, 2022, he achieved his first career triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 111–110 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news |title=Raptors' Scottie Barnes: Triple-double despite loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-scottie-barnes-triple-double-despite-loss/ |access-date=November 7, 2022 |agency=RotoWire Staff |work=CBS Sports |date=November 5, 2022}} He was named to the [[2023 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|2023]] [[Rising Stars Challenge]]. The Raptors were eliminated from playoff contention on April 12 in a play-in game against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Barnes had 19 points and 10 rebounds in the 109–105 loss.{{Cite web |date=2023-04-12 |title=LaVine scores 39, Bulls beat Raptors 109-105 in play-in game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401539673 |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He exhibited what media writers considered a [[sophomore slump]] as, compared to his rookie year, he averaged the same 15.3 points per game while his rebounds per game dropped from 7.5 to 6.0. His field goal percentage decreased from 49.2% to 45.6%,{{Cite news |last=Ibrahim |first=Abdulhamid |date=2023-10-06 |title='I love passing': Raptors' Scottie Barnes embracing chance to play more point guard |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/nba-toronto-raptors-scottie-barnes-point-guard-1.6988910 |access-date=2026-05-23 |work=[[CBC News]] |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}} with notable declines in effectiveness for shots from "[[Basketball moves#Tear drop|floater]] range" and jump shots from multiple ranges. His playmaking was an area of improvement,{{Cite news |last=Koreen |first=Eric |last2=Partnow |first2=Seth |date=2023-05-26 |title=How should the Raptors view Scottie Barnes’ sophomore slump? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4552686/2023/05/26/raptors-scottie-barnes-slump/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207021048/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4552686/2023/05/26/raptors-scottie-barnes-slump/ |archive-date=2024-12-07 |access-date=2026-05-24 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} with his assists per game increasing from 3.5 to 4.8. ====Breakthrough and first All-Star appearance (2023–2024)==== The off-season saw the departure of Raptors point guard [[Fred VanVleet]] and head coach [[Nick Nurse]]. Barnes was more involved in ball-handling and playmaking under new head coach [[Darko Rajaković]].{{Cite web |last=Lewenberg |first=Josh |date=2024-01-19 |title=Barnes to lead Raptors into post-Siakam era as face of franchise |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/lewenberg-barnes-to-lead-raptors-into-post-siakam-era-as-face-of-franchise-1.2064865 |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |language=en}} He scored 20 or more points six times during the first seven games—it took him 30 games to do so the previous season. His strong start was underscored in a 123–116 comeback victory against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on November 5, 2023, during which he recorded 30 points with five completed three-pointers, 11 rebounds, six assists, three steals and three blocks.{{Cite web |last=Lewenberg |first=Josh |date=2023-11-07 |title=How Barnes’ emergence impacts Raptors’ decision-making moving forward |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/how-scottie-barnes-emergence-impacts-toronto-raptors-decision-making-moving-forward-1.2032706 |access-date=2026-05-25 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]]}} The Raptors traded [[OG Anunoby]] and [[Pascal Siakam]] by mid-season, which cemented Barnes as the [[Franchise player|franchise cornerstone]]. General manager [[Masai Ujiri]] said Barnes' breakthrough year was a motivator for the team to make the trades. Barnes was named as an injury replacement player for [[Joel Embiid]] for the [[2024 NBA All-Star Game]], which was his first All-Star selection. Regarded as a defense-oriented star and one of the most versatile defenders in the NBA, Barnes is capable of guarding players of all five positions and of various skill sets, often being assigned to the best offensive player of the opposing team indiscriminately. He can provide rim protection, off-ball defense and one-on-one perimeter guarding, and can easily shift between roles. While capable of many assignments, Barnes is most impactful off-ball as a roamer who can provide help defense and disrupt offensive sets with anticipative plays.{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=Blake |date=2023-11-21 |title=Mirror images of the same idea, Raptors and Magic set for tournament clash |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/mirror-images-of-the-same-idea-raptors-and-magic-set-for-tournament-clash/ |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}} In the scoring department, Barnes had been described as "relatively limited" and "not a natural scorer".{{Cite web |last=Brener |first=Jeremy |date=2026-03-09 |title=Scottie Barnes Has Been Excellent, But He Could Hold Raptors Back |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/onsi/news/scottie-barnes-has-been-excellent-but-he-could-hold-toronto-raptors-back |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}} Weak three-point shooting and an inconsistent jump shot are considered his biggest weaknesses. He shot only 30% from three-point range through his first five seasons in the NBA.{{Cite news |last=Koreen |first=Eric |date=2026-04-24 |title=Scottie Barnes’ first playoff masterpiece shows Raptors forward’s all-around brilliance |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7224459/2026/04/24/raptors-scottie-barnes-playoff-masterpiece-cavaliers/ |url-access=limited |access-date=2026-06-02 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Regarding his shooting form, Steven Loung of [[Sportsnet]] wrote in 2021: "He's very stilted between the transfer of crouching down to going up with the ball, his elbow is looks to drift to the side and his release is pretty slow." Without reliability in either aspect, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' suggested Barnes is better suited as a secondary scoring option on a team rather than the leader. To develop his shot, Barnes doubled his mid-range field goal attempts during the 2024–25 season and showed "emerging outlines of a go-to jumper in the mid-range". He improved his mid-range shooting by the 2025–26 season in his best career shooting year thus far,{{Cite news |last=Koreen |first=Eric |date=2026-03-30 |title=Scottie Barnes’ impact on Raptors merits spot on one of the three All-NBA teams |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7157069/2026/03/30/scottie-barnes-toronto-raptors-awards-all-nba/ |url-access=limited |access-date=2026-06-15 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} although this was also attributed to a more efficient shot diet. ==Personal life== Barnes' father, Scott Barnes Sr., is Jamaican, and many of his relatives are Canadian.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-07-30 |title='I'm trying to achieve greatness': Raptors draft pick Scottie Barnes willing to work |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/im-trying-to-achieve-greatness-raptors-draft-pick-scottie-barnes-willing-to-work/ |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=[[CTV News]] |language=en |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}} In September 2024, he and his partner, Alyssa Rae Holmes, announced they had welcomed a daughter.{{Cite web |last=Laskaris |first=Adam |date=2024-10-08 |title=Scottie Barnes back with Raptors after birth of his child |url=https://dailyhive.com/toronto/raptors-scottie-barnes-child |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=[[Daily Hive]] |language=en}} Outside of basketball, Barnes is an avid [[gamer]]: his favourite video games are the [[NBA 2K]] franchise. He often livestreams himself playing the games on [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]]. He also enjoys [[theatre]], particularly the musical [[Hamilton (musical)|Hamilton]], viewing it in [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] whenever he visits [[New York City]]. He became a fan of theatre in 2023 after viewing Hamilton on the suggestion of Toronto Raptors assistant coach [[Jama Mahlalela]]. Since then he has viewed many plays and musicals. He and teammate [[Jamal Shead]] appeared in a [[National Ballet of Canada]] production of "[[The Nutcracker]]" in Toronto on December 19, 2025, in non-dancing cameo roles.{{Cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=2026-01-30 |title=Raptors forward Scottie Barnes falls in love with theater: 'It's become a part of his identity' |url=https://andscape.com/features/raptors-forward-scottie-barnes-falls-in-love-with-theater-its-become-a-part-of-his-identity/ |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=[[Andscape]] |language=en-US}} ==
